data.content_ref: inline:The target commits an internal contradiction: its mechanism explicitly states that corroboration is 'a report of past performance, carrying no probability for the future,' yet in the same sentence labels the preference for high-corroboration theories as 'the best available guess at truth.' If corroboration genuinely carries no information about future performance or truth-likeness, then selecting on its basis is epistemically arbitrary with respect to verisimilitude — it cannot be 'the best available guess at truth' any more than a coin flip can. The phrase 'best available guess at truth' smuggles in the assumption that past corroboration is positively related to future truth-likeness, which is precisely the inductive inference the target claims to avoid. The target's own countercondition — 'If the metaphysical faith required is indistinguishable from the principle of uniformity of nature, the distinction from induction is merely verbal' — is merely listed and never refuted. The mechanism demonstrates why it cannot be refuted: the jump from 'no probability for the future' to 'best guess at truth' requires exactly the uniformity-of-nature premise that constitutes induction.
